samples.task_summary: Predicting taxi-related outcomes under distribution shift using features that should generalize across train/test domains.
samples.rationale: Month can capture broad seasonality and weather/holiday effects, but it is also a weak proxy for domain-specific temporal drift and may not remain stable across splits, so its marginal predictive value is limited.

samples.task_summary: Predict taxi trip demand or related ride outcome under distribution shift across time and domains.
samples.rationale: Month can capture broad seasonality in taxi demand, but it is also a coarse time marker that is highly domain- and split-dependent, so its predictive value is limited and potentially brittle under shift.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip belongs to the target label in the whyshift taxi domain-generalization benchmark using trip metadata.
samples.rationale: Month can capture broad seasonality in taxi demand, but it is also a strong domain/time marker that may shift across splits and is unlikely to be a robust causal predictor on its own.

samples.task_summary: Predict taxi trip demand or related ride outcomes under distribution shift using trip context features.
samples.rationale: Month can capture broad seasonality in taxi usage, but it is a weak and potentially brittle proxy that may reflect dataset collection periods or shifting calendar effects rather than a stable causal signal.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip will be profitable or high-demand under distribution shift using trip context and timing.
samples.rationale: Month can capture broad seasonality in taxi demand and weather-related travel patterns, but it is also a coarse temporal proxy that may shift across domains and can reflect dataset-specific sampling artifacts rather than stable causal structure.

samples.task_summary: Predicting taxi trip outcomes in a way that should generalize across shifts in the data distribution.
samples.rationale: Week of year can capture broad seasonality in taxi demand and travel patterns, but it is a weak and fairly brittle proxy that may reflect dataset-specific time splits or holiday effects rather than stable causal structure.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip will be high-demand under distribution shift across time and/or location domains.
samples.rationale: Week of year can capture broad seasonal demand patterns, but it is a coarse time index that is often confounded with domain split and calendar-specific artifacts; its predictive value is likely unstable across train/test shifts.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip will be in the target outcome under distribution shift using trip context features.
samples.rationale: Week of year can capture broad seasonality in taxi demand, but it is a weak and potentially domain-specific time proxy that may not transfer reliably across train/test splits compared with more directly causal trip context.

samples.task_summary: Predicting taxi-related outcomes from trip context under distribution shift across environments.
samples.rationale: Pickup week may capture broad seasonal demand patterns, but it is a coarse calendar marker that is often tied to domain-specific time shifts and dataset collection periods rather than a stable causal signal, so its usefulness should be limited.

samples.task_summary: Predicting taxi trip demand or related outcome under distribution shift across time/domain splits.
samples.rationale: Week of year can capture broad seasonality and holiday/weather-related demand patterns that may transfer somewhat, but it is also a coarse temporal proxy that can overfit to dataset-specific calendar shifts and domain boundaries, so its stable marginal usefulness is limited.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip is in the minority/shifted group under the whyshift taxi benchmark using trip metadata that should generalize across domains.
samples.rationale: Day of week can capture real demand and travel-pattern differences, but it is a weak and potentially brittle proxy that may vary across domains and is less semantically stable than core trip attributes.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip will be high-value or otherwise meet the benchmark’s target using trip attributes that generalize across domains.
samples.rationale: Day of week can capture stable demand patterns like commuting and weekend travel, so it may be moderately predictive across shifts. However, it is only an indirect proxy and can also reflect dataset-specific temporal sampling, so it should not be treated as highly reliable.

samples.task_summary: Predicting taxi trip duration from pickup-related trip attributes under distribution shift.
samples.rationale: Day of week can weakly reflect stable travel patterns like weekday vs. weekend traffic, but it is mostly a coarse temporal proxy and is less directly tied to trip duration than spatial or time-of-day factors; its predictive value should be limited and potentially shift across domains.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip will be long or short under distribution shift.
samples.rationale: Day of week can weakly affect trip patterns through commuting and weekend travel, but it is a coarse temporal proxy that is not inherently causal and may vary across domains, so its stable predictive value should be limited.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip will be long or short from trip context features under distribution shift.
samples.rationale: Day of week can capture some stable demand and traffic patterns, but it is a weak proxy and may reflect dataset-specific temporal shifts rather than a robust causal signal.

samples.task_summary: Predicting a taxi trip outcome in the whyshift taxi benchmark using trip metadata under distribution shift.
samples.rationale: Pickup hour can capture stable demand and traffic patterns that affect taxi outcomes, but it is only moderately predictive and can also reflect time-specific spurious correlations that may shift across domains.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip belongs to the shifted target class in the whyshift taxi benchmark using trip metadata that should generalize across environments.
samples.rationale: Pickup hour can capture stable demand patterns like rush hour, nightlife, and commuting behavior, which may remain predictive across domains. It is not a direct identifier or obvious leakage feature, but it can also reflect location-specific temporal quirks and seasonal artifacts, so its usefulness is moderate rather than high.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip belongs to the target outcome in the whyshift taxi domain-shift benchmark using trip attributes that should generalize across environments.
samples.rationale: Pickup hour can capture stable demand patterns such as rush hour and nighttime effects, which are plausibly predictive across domains, but it is also prone to environment-specific temporal and operational shifts, so it should be useful but not overly trusted.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip belongs to the target distribution shift setting in the whyshift taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Pickup hour is a semantically meaningful driver of taxi demand and trip patterns, so it should retain predictive value across domains, though it may also capture some time-specific seasonal or operational artifacts.

samples.task_summary: Predicting the taxi fare or related trip outcome from ride attributes in the whyshift taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Pickup hour can capture stable demand and traffic patterns that affect trip duration and fare, but it is also a weak proxy for time-specific, city-specific, and shift-dependent artifacts that may not generalize well across domains.

samples.task_summary: Predict a taxi-related target from pickup context under distribution shift.
samples.rationale: Time of day is a broadly stable signal for taxi demand and trip patterns, capturing regular commuting, nightlife, and rush-hour effects that should generalize better than location-specific shortcuts. It is not a direct domain identifier, though it can still pick up some dataset-specific temporal artifacts.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip belongs to the target distribution shift setting in the whyshift taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Pickup time is a plausible stable driver of taxi demand and trip patterns across domains, so it should retain predictive value; however, exact minute-of-day can also capture brittle temporal quirks and schedule-specific artifacts, so it is useful but not maximally robust.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip belongs to the out-of-distribution target under the benchmark's ride-related prediction task.
samples.rationale: Pickup time can capture stable diurnal demand patterns and traffic/behavior cycles that often generalize across splits, but it can also act as a proxy for domain-specific temporal shifts, so it is useful yet not fully robust.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip outcome or label generalizes across different environments using trip-related inputs.
samples.rationale: Time of day can be genuinely predictive of taxi demand and trip patterns, but it is also a strong proxy for domain-specific temporal shifts, rush-hour effects, and dataset collection artifacts, so its stability across train/test domains is only moderate.

samples.task_summary: Predicting a taxi trip outcome from pickup-related attributes in the whyshift taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Time of day is a semantically meaningful driver of taxi demand, traffic, and trip patterns, so it should transfer reasonably across domains; however, it can also pick up dataset-specific temporal sampling shifts and seasonality, so it is useful but not perfectly invariant.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip outcome or label generalizes across different domain shifts in the taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Trip distance is a core causal driver of taxi fares, duration, and trip characteristics, so it should remain predictive across domains; it is not an obvious identifier or leakage feature, though its effect may vary somewhat with geography and routing patterns.

samples.task_summary: Predict the target outcome for NYC taxi trips under distribution shift, using features that should remain informative across domains.
samples.rationale: Trip distance is a core causal driver of taxi fare and trip duration, and its relationship to the target should remain stable across train/test domains with little risk of leakage or domain-specific shortcutting.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip will be completed successfully across different environments/domains in the whyshift taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Trip distance is a direct, semantically meaningful driver of taxi outcomes and should remain predictive across domains, with little indication of leakage or domain-specific shortcut behavior.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip outcome is positive under distribution shift across different domains.
samples.rationale: Trip distance is a core causal driver of taxi trip duration and fare-related outcomes, so it should remain broadly predictive across domains; it is not an obvious identifier or leakage feature, though its effect may vary somewhat with geography and routing patterns.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip outcome is positive in a way that should generalize across domain shifts in the taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Trip distance is a direct, semantically meaningful driver of taxi outcomes and is likely to remain predictive across environments, though its effect can vary with local geography and routing patterns.

samples.task_summary: Predict whether a taxi trip will be in the shifted test domain using trip characteristics that remain meaningful across environments.
samples.rationale: Travel direction can capture genuine route structure and city geography, so it may carry some stable signal, but it is also highly context-dependent and can reflect domain-specific routing patterns or spurious correlations rather than a robust causal factor.

samples.task_summary: Predicting a taxi trip outcome in the whyshift taxi benchmark using features that should generalize across train and test domains.
samples.rationale: Travel direction may capture some stable spatial structure in trip patterns, but it is often a weak proxy for route, location, or time-specific demand and can shift with geography, traffic, and sampling; thus it offers limited but nonzero robust predictive value.

samples.task_summary: Predict a taxi trip outcome in a way that should generalize across train/test shifts in the taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Trip direction can capture some stable route geometry and city layout effects, but by itself it is a weak proxy for the target and may reflect domain-specific travel patterns or spurious correlations rather than broadly invariant signal.

samples.task_summary: Predicting a taxi ride outcome in the whyshift taxi benchmark from trip attributes under distribution shift.
samples.rationale: Trip direction can carry some stable signal because travel orientation may correlate with route geometry and destination patterns, but it is also highly context-dependent and can act as a brittle proxy for location, neighborhood, or domain-specific traffic patterns rather than a robust causal feature.

samples.task_summary: Predict the taxi ride outcome in a way that should generalize across shifting environments in the whyshift taxi benchmark.
samples.rationale: Trip direction can be genuinely related to route length, traffic patterns, and destination geography, so it may carry stable signal, but it is also a weak proxy for location-specific and time-specific artifacts that can shift across domains.
